tools.name: submit_total_loss_intake
tools.description: Submit a vehicle owner's total-loss situation to SecondAppraisal on their behalf. Minimum: one of customer.phone / customer.email, your `agent` self-identification, a `consent.attestation`, and `consent.owner_authorization` (the fixed sentence, word for word). Returns a receipt with `customer_confir

tools.name: get_intake_status
tools.description: Fetch the current receipt for a submitted intake (status, confirm link while still confirmable, preliminary).

tools.name: upload_valuation_report
tools.description: Attach the insurer's Market Valuation Report (CCC / Mitchell PDF) to a submitted intake. We parse it (vehicle, mileage, offer, insurer, loss date) and refresh the preliminary. Allow up to two minutes.

tools.name: get_preliminary_estimate
tools.description: A no-commitment early market read for a vehicle: comparable listing prices near the customer (10th percentile / median / 90th), an odometer-adjusted mid, and the gap vs the insurer's offer. Not an appraisal. Nothing is stored about the customer.

tools.name: get_state_total_loss_rules
tools.description: State-specific total-loss facts: threshold and method, whether an independent appraiser must be licensed there, whether third-party appraisals are allowed, statute citations, must-know rights, common pitfalls, and the consumer hotline. For New York and Vermont, appraiser_license_required is null bec

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "submit_total_loss_intake" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "submit_total_loss_intake" is 1457 chars, far longer than this server's median (245). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "submit_total_loss_intake" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_total_loss_intake · Private data: submit_total_loss_intake · Public sink: submit_total_loss_intake, upload_valuation_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_total_loss_intake · Private data: submit_total_loss_intake · Public sink: submit_total_loss_intake, upload_valuation_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
